## Level of the Fieller difference interval {#sec-ratio-difference-level}

The Fieller difference interval in (-@eq-fieller-difference-coverage) combines two treatment-group-specific Fieller sets, each constructed at level $1-\alpha/2$, and controls their joint error through Bonferroni's inequality.
This appendix asks whether the Bonferroni correction can be dropped, so that each treatment-group-specific set is instead constructed at level $1-\alpha$.
We prove that the resulting interval has asymptotic coverage at least $1-\alpha$ along every regular-denominator sequence and that this lower bound is sharp.
The corresponding uniform claim over weak as well as regular denominators reduces to the Gaussian overlap conjecture stated in @sec-ratio-difference-general; it is not established by the argument below.

To treat both constructions at once, fix a per-group critical value $w>0$ and define
$$
C_{d,n}^{\mathrm F}(w)
=
\left\{
r\in\mathbb R:
|\widehat v_{d,n}(r)|
\leq
\frac{w}{\sqrt n}
\widehat\sigma_{v,d,n}(r)
\right\},
\qquad d\in\{0,1\},
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-arm-set}
together with
$$
C_n^{\mathrm F}(w)
=
\begin{cases}
\mathbb R,
& T_n^z\leq w, \\[2ex]
\left[
\inf C_{1,n}^{\mathrm F}(w)-\sup C_{0,n}^{\mathrm F}(w),
\quad
\sup C_{1,n}^{\mathrm F}(w)-\inf C_{0,n}^{\mathrm F}(w)
\right],
& T_n^z>w.
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-family}
The Bonferroni interval is $C_n^{\mathrm F}(z_{1-\alpha/4})$.
The uncorrected interval is $C_n^{\mathrm F}(z_{1-\alpha/2})$.
The argument leading to (-@eq-treatment-group-fieller-coverage), with $z_{1-\alpha/2}$ in place of $z_{1-\alpha/4}$, gives
$$
\limsup_{n\to\infty}
\sup_{\boldsymbol\theta\in\Theta}
\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\theta}
\left(r_{d,n}\notin C_{d,n}^{\mathrm F}(z_{1-\alpha/2})\right)
\leq
\alpha,
\qquad d\in\{0,1\}.
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-arm-coverage}
This marginal statement alone does not control the difference interval at level $1-\alpha$.

### An overlap characterization {#sec-ratio-difference-overlap}

Write
$$
W_{d,n}(r)
=
\frac{\sqrt n\,\widehat v_{d,n}(r)}
{\widehat\sigma_{v,d,n}(r)}.
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-pivot}
On $\{T_n^z>w\}$, both treatment-group-specific sets are bounded intervals and $C_n^{\mathrm F}(w)$ is their Minkowski difference.
Because $r_n=r_{1,n}-r_{0,n}$,
$$
r_n\in C_n^{\mathrm F}(w)
\iff
\exists\,x\in\mathbb R:
\quad
\begin{gathered}
r_{1,n}+x\in C_{1,n}^{\mathrm F}(w), \\
r_{0,n}+x\in C_{0,n}^{\mathrm F}(w).
\end{gathered}
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-common-shift}
Consequently, on this bounded branch,
$$
r_n\in C_n^{\mathrm F}(w)
\iff
\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}
\max
\left\{
|W_{0,n}(r_{0,n}+x)|,
|W_{1,n}(r_{1,n}+x)|
\right\}
\leq w.
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-profiled}
The full coverage event also includes the automatic-coverage branch:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\{r_n\in C_n^{\mathrm F}(w)\}
={}&\{T_n^z\leq w\} \\
&\cup
\left(
\{T_n^z>w\}
\cap
\left\{
\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}
\max_{d\in\{0,1\}}
|W_{d,n}(r_{d,n}+x)|
\leq w
\right\}
\right).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-full-coverage-event}
Evaluating the maximum in (-@eq-ratio-difference-profiled) at $x=0$ recovers the Bonferroni bound.
The infimum over the common displacement is the slack that this bound discards.

### Regular denominators {#sec-ratio-difference-regular}

Consider an arbitrary sequence $\boldsymbol\theta_n\in\Theta$ satisfying (-@eq-ratio-regular-denominator-condition), and write $\widehat r_{d,n}=\overline Y_{d,n}/\overline Z_{d,n}$.
For every displacement $x$,
$$
\widehat v_{d,n}(r_{d,n}+x)
=
\overline Z_{d,n}
(\widehat r_{d,n}-r_{d,n}-x).
$$
The triangle and reverse triangle inequalities for the covariance norm give
$$
\left|
\widehat\sigma_{v,d,n}(r_{d,n}+x)
-
\widehat\sigma_{v,d,n}(\widehat r_{d,n})
\right|
\leq
|x-(\widehat r_{d,n}-r_{d,n})|
\widehat\sigma_{z,d,n}.
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-scale-bound}
Recall that
$$
T_{d,n}^z
=
\frac{\sqrt n\,|\overline Z_{d,n}|}
{\widehat\sigma_{z,d,n}},
\qquad
\widehat\sigma_{\ell,d,n}
=
\frac{\widehat\sigma_{v,d,n}(\widehat r_{d,n})}
{|\overline Z_{d,n}|}.
$$
On $\{T_{d,n}^z>w\}$, (-@eq-ratio-difference-scale-bound) yields the deterministic inclusions
$$
\begin{aligned}
&\left[
\widehat r_{d,n}-r_{d,n}
-
\frac{w\widehat\sigma_{\ell,d,n}}
{\sqrt n(1+w/T_{d,n}^z)},
\quad
\widehat r_{d,n}-r_{d,n}
+
\frac{w\widehat\sigma_{\ell,d,n}}
{\sqrt n(1+w/T_{d,n}^z)}
\right] \\
&\qquad\subseteq
C_{d,n}^{\mathrm F}(w)-r_{d,n} \\
&\qquad\subseteq
\left[
\widehat r_{d,n}-r_{d,n}
-
\frac{w\widehat\sigma_{\ell,d,n}}
{\sqrt n(1-w/T_{d,n}^z)},
\quad
\widehat r_{d,n}-r_{d,n}
+
\frac{w\widehat\sigma_{\ell,d,n}}
{\sqrt n(1-w/T_{d,n}^z)}
\right].
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-arm-sandwich}
For example, the inner inclusion follows by combining the lower bound in (-@eq-ratio-difference-scale-bound) with the defining Fieller inequality; the outer inclusion follows from the corresponding upper bound.

The argument in @sec-estimated-denominator-strength gives $T_n^z\stackrel{\mathcal P}{\to}\infty$ along the chosen sequence.
Therefore both treatment-group-specific sets are bounded with probability approaching one, and (-@eq-ratio-difference-arm-sandwich) shows that their endpoints differ from
$$
\widehat r_{d,n}-r_{d,n}
\mathbin{\pm}
\frac{w\widehat\sigma_{\ell,d,n}}{\sqrt n}
$$
by $o_{\mathcal P}(\widehat\sigma_{\ell,d,n}/\sqrt n)$.
Taking pairwise differences and using (-@eq-ratio-robust-scale), the endpoints of $C_n^{\mathrm F}(w)-r_n$ consequently differ from
$$
\widehat r_n-r_n
\mathbin{\pm}
\frac{w\widehat\sigma_{r,n}}{\sqrt n}
$$
by $o_{\mathcal P}(\widehat\sigma_{r,n}/\sqrt n)$.
Thus the uncorrected Fieller difference interval and the delta-method interval in (-@eq-ratio-delta-method-interval) are asymptotically equivalent along every regular-denominator sequence.

To state the resulting coverage correctly for a triangular array, use compactness of $[0,1]$ to take a further subsequence along which $\omega_n\to\omega\in[0,1]$.
Equations (-@eq-ratio-feasible-normal-approximation) and (-@eq-ratio-conservative-variance) imply
$$
\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\theta_n}
\left(r_n\in C_n^{\mathrm F}(z_{1-\alpha/2})\right)
=
\begin{cases}
2\Phi\!\left(z_{1-\alpha/2}/\omega\right)-1,
& \omega>0, \\[1ex]
1,
& \omega=0.
\end{cases}
+o(1).
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-regular-coverage}
Since $\omega\leq1$, every such subsequential limit is at least $1-\alpha$.
It follows that, for every sequence satisfying (-@eq-ratio-regular-denominator-condition),
$$
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\theta_n}
\left(r_n\in C_n^{\mathrm F}(z_{1-\alpha/2})\right)
\geq
1-\alpha.
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-regular-validity}

### Sharpness {#sec-ratio-difference-sharp}

The bound in (-@eq-ratio-difference-regular-validity) is sharp.
Equality in (-@eq-ratio-conservative-variance) holds when the oracle scores are positively proportional.
Since
$$
\ell_{i,d,n}
=
\frac{y_{i,d}-r_{d,n}z_{i,d}}{\overline z_{d,n}},
$$
the corresponding correlation condition is
$$
\operatorname{Corr}
\left(
y_{i,1}-r_{1,n}z_{i,1},
y_{i,0}-r_{0,n}z_{i,0}
\right)
\operatorname{sign}(\overline z_{1,n}\overline z_{0,n})
=1.
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-sharp-condition}
In particular, when both denominator means have the same sign, the projected outcomes must be perfectly positively correlated; when the means have opposite signs, they must be perfectly negatively correlated.

For a concrete admissible triangular array, set $p=1/2$ and, for each $n$, choose bounded, centered finite-population vectors $\{\epsilon_{i,n}\}_{i=1}^n$, $\{\zeta_{i,0,n}\}_{i=1}^n$, and $\{\zeta_{i,1,n}\}_{i=1}^n$.
Suppose their variances are bounded above and away from zero, $\epsilon_{i,n}$ is uncorrelated with each $\zeta_{i,d,n}$, and their maximum variance shares converge to zero.
Let
$$
z_{i,d}=1+\zeta_{i,d,n},
\qquad
y_{i,d}=r_dz_{i,d}+\epsilon_{i,n},
\qquad d\in\{0,1\}.
$$
Then $\overline z_{d,n}=1$, the regular-denominator condition holds, both within-group covariance matrices are positive definite, and
$$
\ell_{i,0,n}=\ell_{i,1,n}=\epsilon_{i,n}.
$$
Consequently $\omega_n=1$, and (-@eq-ratio-difference-regular-coverage) gives
$$
\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\theta_n}
\left(r_n\in C_n^{\mathrm F}(z_{1-\alpha/2})\right)
=
1-\alpha+o(1).
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-sharp-coverage}
This proves that no uniform lower bound strictly greater than $1-\alpha$ is possible, even within the regular-denominator regime.

@fig-ratio-difference-level-sharpness illustrates this sharpness mechanism at finite $n$.
The simulation uses strong, symmetric denominators and varies the correlation between the two projected outcomes.
In this configuration, the uncorrected interval's non-coverage approaches $\alpha$ as the correlation approaches one, while the Bonferroni interval remains conservative.

![Non-coverage of the nominal $95\%$ Fieller difference interval as the cross-group projected-outcome correlation varies, with strong symmetric denominators. The uncorrected interval (each group at level $1-\alpha$) approaches the sharp value $\alpha$; the Bonferroni interval (each group at level $1-\alpha/2$) remains conservative.](ratio_difference_level_sharpness.png){#fig-ratio-difference-level-sharpness}

### General denominators {#sec-ratio-difference-general}

The preceding proof does not cover sequences with bounded denominator strength.
For such sequences, the treatment-group-specific sets can be unbounded or asymmetric, and the deterministic sandwich (-@eq-ratio-difference-arm-sandwich) does not approach the delta-method interval.
The exact limiting problem can nevertheless be stated explicitly.

For each treatment group, standardize the projected sample-mean error and denominator error to obtain a jointly Gaussian limit $(A_d,B_d)$ with unit marginal variances and correlation $\psi_d$.
Let
$$
\lambda_d
=
\lim
\frac{\sqrt n\,\overline z_{d,n}}
{\sigma_{z,d,n}},
\qquad
\Lambda_d=\lambda_d+B_d.
$$
In the nondimensional coordinate
$$
s
=
(r-r_{d,n})
\frac{\sigma_{z,d,n}}
{\sigma_{v,d,n}(r_{d,n})},
$$
the limiting Fieller set is
$$
I_d(w)
=
\left\{
s\in\mathbb R:
(\Lambda_d^2-w^2)s^2
-2(\Lambda_dA_d-w^2\psi_d)s
+A_d^2-w^2
\leq0
\right\}.
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-limit-quadratic}
The identity
$$
\begin{aligned}
&(\Lambda_dA_d-w^2\psi_d)^2
-(\Lambda_d^2-w^2)(A_d^2-w^2) \\
&\qquad=
w^2\left[
(A_d-\psi_d\Lambda_d)^2
+(1-\psi_d^2)(\Lambda_d^2-w^2)
\right]
\end{aligned}
$$
shows that $I_d(w)$ is a bounded nonempty interval whenever $|\Lambda_d|>w$.
When $|\Lambda_d|\leq w$, the procedure uses the automatic-coverage branch.

Only the relative scale matters.
After extracting a further subsequence and normalizing the control scale to one, let $\kappa\in[0,\infty]$ denote the limiting treatment-to-control scale ratio.
The boundary values correspond to one treatment-group-specific scale dominating the other.
The full uniform claim would follow from the following Gaussian overlap inequality:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P\Bigg(&
|\Lambda_0|\leq w
\ \text{or}\
|\Lambda_1|\leq w \\
&\ \text{or}\
I_0(w)
\cap
\kappa I_1(w)
\neq\varnothing
\Bigg)
\geq
2\Phi(w)-1
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ratio-difference-gaussian-conjecture}
for every admissible joint Gaussian law of $(A_0,B_0,A_1,B_1)$, including singular limits, every pair of finite strengths, and every $\kappa\in[0,\infty]$, with the boundary cases interpreted by limits.
At $w=z_{1-\alpha/2}$, the right-hand side is $1-\alpha$.

Equation (-@eq-ratio-difference-gaussian-conjecture) is a conjecture, not a consequence of the marginal Fieller coverage result or of Bonferroni's inequality.
The regular-denominator proof establishes its infinite-strength boundary, and (-@eq-ratio-difference-sharp-coverage) shows that its proposed lower bound would be sharp.
A proof for finite strengths would require this new Gaussian interval-overlap inequality, followed by a uniform joint four-dimensional Gaussian approximation, consistent covariance standardization, and a subsequence argument that also handles singular Gaussian limits and boundary events.
Without that result, the analysis does not justify replacing the Bonferroni interval in the main construction when uniform validity over weak denominators is required.
